subject: Scheduling keystore rotation windows, proxy latency SLA & emergency unseal protocol

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>

Subject: Scheduling keystore rotation windows, proxy latency SLA & emergency unseal protocol

Hi team (Acme + Redwood),

We're kicking off the conversation about regular keystore rotation and the proxy SLA for your on-prem deployment. Goals for this thread: agree on an operational rotation window that minimizes app impact, confirm proxy latency targets and fallback behavior, and document the emergency unseal protocol (who has custodial keys, TTLs, and the steps to get services back online).

Attached: rotation-matrix.xlsx (proposed windows by region), proxy-latency-diagram.png (current proxy topology). Also see a quick DP QA checklist in the attachments for what we'll validate during a rotation.

Questions to get started:
- What maintenance windows do you typically allow for network-adjacent infra (weekly vs monthly; prefer overnight local time)?
- Can Acme tolerate up to a 3-minute soft outage for a planned rotation if we stagger nodes, or do we need a zero-second SLA for rolling restarts?
- Who will be the on-site custodian that can physically access HSM console or KMS operator escape hatch in an emergency? (Provide name and contact.)

Proposed times (PT):
- Weekly short window: Tue 02:00–03:00 PT (30–45m ops work + validation)
- Monthly full rotation: 2nd Sat 01:00–04:00 PT (3h maintenance)

Please reply with availability and any hard constraints. Once we align, we'll produce a mutually-agreed rotation runbook and schedule an acceptance rehearsal.

Thanks,

Markus Klein
Head of Platform Security
Redwood Inference

Attachments: rotation-matrix.xlsx, proxy-latency-diagram.png

From: Acme Health Infra <infra-ops@acmehealth.com>

Cc: hannah.schmitt@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Scheduling keystore rotation windows, proxy latency SLA & emergency unseal protocol

Markus — thanks for the clear kickoff. Quick answers from the Acme side:

- Maintenance windows: Our standard is Sun 01:00–04:00 local (EST) for full infra changes, and weekdays 03:00–04:00 for brief operations. We can open Tue 02:00–03:00 PT as an exception for staggered work but prefer keeping the monthly window on Sundays.
- SLA tolerance: For clinical workloads we need user-visible availability to remain within 10s for most operations. We can accept a short degraded state for background batch inference, but frontdoor latency >10s is a no-go. So zero perceived downtime for frontdoor — any rotation must preserve the front proxy path.
- On-site custodian: Lisa Hernandez (lisa.hernandez@acmehealth.com) is the on-call facilities lead with HSM console access. She cannot be on-call 24/7 but will attend rehearsals and be available during scheduled maintenance.

A couple of clarifying items:
1) For emergency unseal: does Redwood provide an operatorless unseal fallback (split-escrow) or do we rely on a single-site custodian?
2) If proxy latency spikes during rotation, do you have automatic model-fallback routes to a hosted variant? Our procurement team wants to understand cost and bandwidth implications.

I'll loop in SecOps (cc Aisha) if you want security reviewers on the thread.

—Lisa
Infra Ops Manager, Acme Health

Thanks Lisa — helpful constraints. A few technical clarifications from our ops/engineering side and a proposed minimal-impact approach: 

1) Emergency unseal model:
- Primary: BYOK with split custody (3-of-5 threshold) where keys are held by a combination of Acme custodians and Redwood escrow. That gives you redundancy without a single-person blast radius.
- Fallback: Operatorless unseal only in fully air-gapped scenarios — otherwise operator-involved due to physical HSM controls and attestation. We can map your custodians into the 3-of-5 set (Lisa + 2 additional Acme delegates + 2 Redwood witnesses).

2) Rotation approach to preserve frontdoor latency:
- Use rolling, per-proxy-prefix rotations: rotate the keystore on a subset of edge proxies at t0 while keeping others serving traffic; healthcheck-based draining prevents frontdoor errors. That keeps perceived latency within your 10s target.
- Staggered windows of 10–15 minutes per proxy-group; overall event fits into the weekly 1-hour short window or monthly 3-hour window depending on scope.

3) Proxy latency spike mitigation & hosted fallback:
- Redwood can configure smart routing: if latency to on-prem proxy exceeds threshold, route to a pinned hosted model (cost applies). Routing rules are policy-driven and we can cap percentage to control cost. We'll include estimated egress and inference costs in the runbook.

I've attached dp-qa-checklist.pdf that includes validation steps (traffic shadowing, KV-cache warmup, and post-rotation fidelity tests).

Proposed immediate next steps:
- Acme confirms 2 additional custodians for split custody list.
- Agree on weekly short window Tue 02:00–03:00 PT as a rehearsal before committing to monthly Sunday rotations.
- Redwood to draft runbook and cost estimate for hosted fallback and share by Thu EOD.

Markus: can you own the runbook draft? Kimberly, please prepare an SLA-exception request template if Acme will require formal sign-off (procurement).

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: dp-qa-checklist.pdf

Lisa / Acme team — thanks for the quick turn. Summarizing decisions so we can formalize and get procurement sign-off: 

Agreed items:
- Rehearsal window: Tue 02:00–03:00 PT (weekly short window) for staggered rotations.
- Monthly rotation: 2nd Sun 01:00–04:00 EST (3-hour maintenance) — Acme to confirm calendar exception.
- Custody model: 3-of-5 split custody. Acme to nominate Lisa + 2 delegates. Redwood will nominate 2 witnesses.
- Frontdoor SLA: Redwood to ensure frontdoor latency <10s via draining and smart-routing; hosted fallback will be used only when thresholds are breached and will be capped at 5% of traffic unless Acme approves higher.

Action items:
- Acme (Lisa): provide 2 additional custodians and preferred contact numbers (by Fri EOD).
- Redwood (Markus): deliver runbook + cost estimate for hosted fallback and the rehearsal play-by-play (by Thu EOD). Link to draft will be posted to Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b-rotation-plan
- Redwood (Kimberly): prepare SLA-exception template and DocuSign for formal approval; will create JIRA ticket SECOPS-7123 for tracking.

If no objections, we'll lock the rehearsal for Tue (two days from now) and run a simulated rotation with no traffic cutover (shadow mode) to verify KV-cache warming and failover behavior. Please reply with explicit sign-off or raise concerns.

Best,

Kimberly Park

Redwood Inference
